name: Expand Perspectives (multi-lens research)
description: Researchers deep-dive an idea from several independent lenses in parallel — first-principles, historical precedent, contrarian/steelman, and second-order effects — then one synthesis pass fans them in into a decision-ready perspective map. A fan-out → fan-in research diamond that widens the option space before the company commits. Complements the orchestrated adaptive-research workflow (use that when the path should adapt; use this when you want breadth in one deterministic pass). Roles routed to the academic division; brain chains editable in the UI.

steps.title: First-principles analysis: {{idea}}
steps.description: Analyze "{{idea}}" from first principles: strip it to the fundamental truths and constraints, rebuild the reasoning from the ground up, and state what MUST be true for it to work. Separate physical/economic laws from conventions that could be broken. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Historical precedent & analogues: {{idea}}
steps.description: Find the historical precedents and analogues for "{{idea}}": who tried something similar, what happened, why they succeeded or failed, and what has changed since that makes the answer different now. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Contrarian steelman: {{idea}}
steps.description: Build the strongest possible case AGAINST "{{idea}}" — the smartest reason a thoughtful skeptic would pass. Then identify which of those objections are fatal vs. addressable, and what evidence would flip each one. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Second-order effects: {{idea}}
steps.description: Map the second- and third-order effects of "{{idea}}" succeeding: who is displaced, what new behaviors emerge, the incentive shifts, and the non-obvious risks and opportunities that appear only downstream. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Synthesize the perspective map: {{idea}}
steps.description: Combine the first-principles, precedent, contrarian, and second-order analyses provided into a single decision-ready perspective map on "{{idea}}": the strongest reasons for and against, where the analyses agree and where they conflict, the crux uncertainty that most changes the answer, and a clear recommendation with the one thing to test first. Output as markdown.
